chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding

a man who prayed Dhuhr in the Masjid al-Shajarah and entered into Ihram, then touched perfume, or hunted game, or had intercourse with his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: There is nothing upon him as long as he has not said the Talbiyyah.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.لَبِّ: To recite the Talbiyyah (declaration of intent)
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid al-Shajarah, a specific location near Mecca associated with the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and Hajj rituals

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for breaking Ihram before reciting Talbiyyah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise temporal boundary for Ihram penalties, establishing that the prohibition of specific acts like using perfume or hunting only becomes binding after the recitation of the Talbiyyah. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the significance of the verbal declaration as the definitive moment of entering the sacred state, distinguishing it from mere intention or physical preparation. Consequently, acts performed prior to this utterance are considered permissible without incurring the financial or sacrificial expiations typically associated with breaking Ihram.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from one of our companions, from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) regarding

a man who Prays Al-Zohr in Masjid Al-Shajarah, and ties the Ihraam, then touches perfume, or hunts a prey, or falls upon his wife. Heasws said: ‘There is nothing upon him for as long as he has not exclaimed Talbiyya’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about

a man who performs al-Zuhr in Masjid al-Shajarah, assumes the state of Ihram, then touches perfumes, or a prey or involves in sexual relation. He (the Imam) said, ‘There is nothing on him because of such things before his saying Talbiyah.’”
